sections.name: Koopa Kid Space
sections.card:
Summary: A space that calls up a Koopa Kid when you land on it, and he then does one of several bad things to you or to everyone. In Mario Party 7 these spaces can only be made by Bowser and Koopa Kid.
Weak points: The space can be removed by placing a different Orb on it, by using Yoshi and Birdo's Egg Orb on it, or when the Star Space moves onto it.
Looks like: A round green space with the Koopa Kid's face in gold at its centre and a golden frame around it.
Tips: The Koopa Kid may give you a Cursed Mushroom so you can roll only 1 to 5 on your next turn, share everyone's coins out evenly, swap coins or places with another player by roulette, make everyone switch places, or shuffle everyone's Orbs. The game always starts with Bowser tossing three Koopa Kid Orbs onto the board, and getting one from an Orb Space or being forced to buy one at Bowser's shop adds another.

sections.name: Chain Chomps on Pyramid Park
sections.card:
Summary: Toadsworth says there are no Stars on Pyramid Park: everyone begins with 5 Stars and you steal them from each other by paying to ride a Chain Chomp and crushing your rivals. The Chain Chomps are found in pyramid dog houses.
Weak points: A Snack Orb, found only on this board, protects you for three turns or until a Chain Chomp attacks.
Looks like: The three Chain Chomps on the right side of the board are black, and the one at the top on the left is a Red Chomp.
Tips: A ride costs 10 coins for one Dice Block or 20 for two, and the Red Chomp gives three Dice Blocks for ten coins; in the last four turns the prices are halved. Matching numbers on the Dice Blocks give no bonus coins while you ride.

sections.name: Bowser Sphinx
sections.card:
Summary: A statue in the centre left of Pyramid Park. When a character lands on the Green Space in front of it, it wakes, thinks you are trying to steal its treasure, and curses everyone with one of three random effects.
Weak points: In Party Cruise its curse is set off by landing on the Green Space in front of it.
Looks like: Its body is modelled on the Great Sphinx of Giza and its head looks like Bowser's, wearing a nemes headdress with pink-and-blue striped lappets and a Chain Chomp ornament.
Tips: The curse is one of three effects for all players: all coins are added up and shared out evenly, Blue and Red Spaces swap for two turns, or Chain Chomp rides cost half as much for two turns. A Whomp blocking the path to the Bowser Sphinx charges 10 coins to let you pass.

sections.name: Dark Star chests
sections.card:
Summary: A black Star hidden in one of the treasure chests that takes one Star from you if you open it. On Grand Canal it is one of the four chests in Blooper's guessing game.
Weak points: None are given; if you choose its chest you must take the Dark Star.
Tips: On Neon Heights, Bowser Time may put a Dark Star in the chest that held the Bob-omb, and paying Koopa Kid to open it makes you take the Dark Star and lose one Star. The Dark Star disappears if the chest with the regular Star is opened first, and unlike in Mario Party 6 you do not lose 20 coins if you have no Stars.

sections.name: Bowser's Lovely Lift!
sections.card:
Summary: A boss minigame against Bowser: you ride an elevator up to the 100th floor while Bowser attacks you. It can only be unlocked in Solo Cruise.
Weak points: You win by reaching the 100th floor, even if Dice Block numbers are left over, and you lose at once if any attack hits you.
Tips: Hit four Dice Blocks each turn and the elevator climbs by the total, between 4 and 40 floors. After the 50th floor a Koopa Kid joins Bowser with the same attacks, three fireballs or three missiles and a laser team attack, and in Solo Cruise the game remembers the floor where you lost so you can resume from there.

sections.name: Hammer Bro Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A yellow Thrown Orb that you set on a space as a trap. An opponent who lands on it loses ten coins to a Hammer Bro, and the coins go to you.
Uses: Place it on a Blue, Red, Character or Koopa Kid Space; it appears on every board except Pyramid Park and Bowser's Enchanted Inferno!.
Tips: It cannot affect the user, and if you land on your own Thrown Orb space you get five coins. A rival under a Metal Mushroom Orb is not harmed by traps.

sections.name: Piranha Plant Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A yellow Thrown Orb trap: an opponent who lands on it is chewed up by a Piranha Plant and loses half their coins, which go to you.
Uses: Place it on a space as a trap; it costs fifteen coins at the Orb Shop and appears on every board except Pagoda Peak and Windmillville.
Tips: If a player is already standing on the space when an opponent lands on it, the Piranha Plant chews only the opponent. You get five coins if you land on your own trap.

sections.name: Spear Guy Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A yellow Thrown Orb trap: an opponent who lands on it has coins stolen by a Spear Guy, as many as a Dice Block roll, and the coins go to you.
Uses: Place it on a chosen space as a trap; it appears on every board except Grand Canal and Neon Heights.
Tips: The Dice Block can roll 5, 10, 20 or 30 coins. This Orb replaces the Goomba Orb from Mario Party 6.

sections.name: Pink Boo Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A yellow Thrown Orb trap: an opponent who lands on it is robbed by a Pink Boo of a Star, or of 20 coins if they have no Stars, and it goes to you.
Uses: Place it on a space as a trap; it appears on every board except Pagoda Peak and Windmillville, and most shops sell it for 30 coins, or 15 on a discount.
Tips: A Pink Boo appears whenever an opponent lands on a Character Space that a Pink Boo Orb made. If you land on your own trap you get five coins.

sections.name: Kamek Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A yellow Thrown Orb trap: if an opponent lands on it, Kamek appears and gives you control of up to three of that opponent's Character Spaces.
Uses: Place it on a space as a trap; it costs ten coins at the Orb Shop and appears on Pagoda Peak, Pyramid Park and Windmillville.
Tips: Kamek takes over the Character Spaces the victim placed on the board, up to three in Mario Party 7. If you land on your own Thrown Orb space you get five coins.

sections.name: Zap Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A red Roadblock Orb with an Amp inside. An opponent who passes the space, not only one who lands on it, is shocked and loses three coins for every space he moves past it.
Uses: Set it on a space as a roadblock; it costs 15 coins at an Orb hut and appears on Pagoda Peak, Neon Heights and Windmillville.
Tips: The effect happens at once, then the space goes back to normal, and you are immune to your own roadblocks. If a player passes another Zap Orb while one is in effect the Zap Orbs stack up, and the effect wears off if the player runs out of coins.

sections.name: Thwomp Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A red Roadblock Orb: an opponent who passes the space is flattened by a Thwomp and must stop moving, which ends their turn.
Uses: Set it on a space as a roadblock; it appears on Pyramid Park, Neon Heights and Windmillville.
Tips: A player under a Metal Mushroom Orb is not stopped: the Thwomp is deflected and the roadblock does nothing. A roadblock disappears once it has been triggered.

sections.name: Metal Mushroom Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A green Self Orb: you turn to metal and are not harmed by the Trap Orbs that rivals put on spaces.
Uses: Use it on yourself to be safe from rivals' traps; it appears on Pagoda Peak, Windmillville and Bowser's Enchanted Inferno!, and costs between five and thirty coins.
Tips: While you are metal a Thwomp Orb is deflected, a Bob-omb Orb is kicked away, and a Tweester Orb dissipates with no effect.

sections.name: Snack Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A green Self Orb found only on Pyramid Park: you use it on yourself and a thrown bone protects you from Chain Chomp attacks.
Uses: Use it on yourself before a Chain Chomp attacks; you are protected for three turns or until a Chain Chomp attacks, which makes you throw the bone automatically.
Tips: Other players on your space are not hit either. In practice it protects you from opponents' attacks for only two of their turn cycles, because turns count down after you move through a Dice Block but opponents can only use Chain Chomps between your turns.

sections.name: Slow 'Shroom Orb
sections.card:
Summary: A green Self Orb that slows the Dice Block right down so you can pick the number you roll.
Uses: Use it on yourself, then hit the button when the number just before the one you want is showing; it appears on every board except Pagoda Peak and Pyramid Park.
Tips: The numbers run upward and start again after 10. For example, to get a three you hit the button when the Dice Block shows a two.
